title: Drone-agnostic sensor-to-map TAK plugin (MISB KLV to georegistered footprints, incremental 3D Tiles and change-vs-baseline overlays on a commodity edge box) with bandwidth-budgeted delta distribution of terrain and basemap packages across TAK federations

scores.rationale: The headline pain (seeing where the drone camera is looking on the TAK map) is already solved for free by ATAK plus the government UAS Tool plugin (FACT, MEDIUM). What remains - waiting hours for cloud 3D when offline without a Skydio/Reveal licence, judging change by eye, stale terrain packages - is real but the corpus and this session's searches found no primary-source AAR or solicitation naming it; the sneakernet-terrain pain was still HYPOTHESIS/LOW after G03's two passes.

Drone flights are daily in DFR programs, wildfire seasons and company sUAS teams, so any residual friction recurs often; but the residual functions (change alerts, terrain refresh) are needed episodically, not on every flight.

No budget line names a sensor-to-map plugin or geospatial delta distribution (Public evidence insufficient). Adjacent money is prime-shaped (AIDP-Next, TITAN, OWT data buy) or program-internal (DHS S&T TAK, TPC). Public-safety users have revealed a zero price point by adopting the free ATAK + UAS Tool + MediaMTX stack. A 1 rather than 0 because SBIR/STRATFI has funded the adjacent product (Reveal) and DHS S&T does pay integrators for TAK features.

ATAK-CIV and TAK Server source are open and a community plugin can be distributed without any contract, so access to users is easy; but there is no office that buys plugins (TPC approval-gated, services-priced), SBIR carries the ownership test, and Army entry runs through AIDP-Next/NGC2 primes.

Every component is open or commodity: MISB KLV parsers, OpenDroneMap/Obj2Tiles to 3D Tiles (FACT, HIGH), Jetson Orin, TAK SDK, CRDT/chunk-manifest sync. The hard parts (incremental reconstruction speed, low-false-alarm change detection, priority scheduling) are engineering, not research.

$250k comfortably buys the unclassified PoC ($60-150k) and a first pilot attempt, but not a defense-validated demo (TAK-GOV/MIL access, exercise participation, clearable field engineer) and not the photogrammetry hire plus 18 months of runway needed to find a paying customer in a free ecosystem.

A lab demo (any KLV feed -> 3D Tiles in minutes -> change overlay -> delta-synced across two federated TAK Servers over a 64 kbit/s emulated link) is achievable in 3-6 months on open data and commercial hardware. Not a 5 because 'credible' for a buyer requires a live user pilot, which needs a sponsor.

Open terrain (USGS 3DEP, Copernicus), open imagery, self-flown KLV video, ATAK-CIV and TAK Server public source cover the entire MVP. Military FMV and OWT are not needed unless the defense variant is pursued, where they are sponsor-gated.

The civil ATAK-CIV product is likely commercial software (EAR99 or 5D002/ENC - RECALL, verify with counsel) with no ATO for agency-run pilots; the defense variant brings TPC MIL-plugin review, possible USML XI questions if adapted for military sensors, and TAK-GOV/MIL distribution control. Medium overall.

A 5 because the scope is unclassified by construction: commercial drones, open data, public TAK source, public-safety first customers; classification dependence is 'none' and no controlled data is required for any MVP milestone.

A 1 because every layer has a free, stock or funded occupant: government UAS Tool (KLV footprint, free), Skydio Onboard Modeling (stock on the Army's company drone), Reveal Farsight (edge 3D to ATAK, USSOCOM-developed, $33.6M STRATFI + $30M Series B, acquisitive), Edgybees (georegistration), OpenDroneMap (free algorithms), DroneSense/DJI/Vision2 (public-safety TAK video), Ditto/CloudTAK/map-depot/AGC RBT (distribution). Only the change-overlay and priority-delta increments are unoccupied.

A 1 because the principal incumbent is government-owned free software with a live roadmap (Cesium 3D Tiles program and AGC RBT demo on the TAK Offsite 2026 agenda, FACT HIGH); it cannot be undercut on price, and the commercial occupants (Skydio, Reveal) are well funded and closer to the users than a new entrant.

Interfaces are open standards (KLV, CoT, 3D Tiles, GeoPackage) and ATAK-CIV SDK is public, but every interface is controlled by someone else (TPC, AGC, drone vendors, Cesium), MIL plugin approval is gated, and the 2026 WinTAK-to-TAKX migration creates maintenance churn.

A 1 because algorithms, interfaces and data are all open and the parent cards' own defensibility sections reach the same conclusion; the only accumulable assets (tuned thresholds, deployed agency servers, TPC relationships) are a head start any of the named incumbents can erase in one or two release cycles.

Wildfire, SAR, disaster, border and inspection TAK users are real and offline-first has appeal, but they already use free stacks and vendor cloud mapping; willingness to pay for a standalone plugin is unproven.

Could expand to allied TAK federations and to more sensor types, but each expansion is another feature inside the same free ecosystem; the realistic ceiling is an Immersive Wisdom-scale niche (single-digit $M/yr, INFERENCE).

Public-safety subscriptions and allied support contracts could recur, but military TAK users do not pay licence fees for plugins and the free baseline erodes renewal leverage; services renewals are the realistic form.

The unclassified scope lets both founders engineer, and the German founder's allied channel is a small plus; but three 'fatal if absent' roles (photogrammetry engineer, TAK ecosystem engineer with TPC relationships, public-safety/SOF domain seller) are missing, SBIR is blocked until the cap table is restructured, and neither founder has flown drones under TAK for a living.

market.summary: No requirement owner, program office or budget line for a sensor-to-map plugin or geospatial delta distribution; the PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER chain breaks at REQUIREMENT OWNER (TPC/AGC/DHS S&T own the roadmap, nobody owns this feature) and at BUDGET (Public evidence insufficient). Public-safety users have revealed a zero price point for the surrounding stack (free ATAK + UAS Tool + MediaMTX); Army money is prime-shaped (AIDP-Next, TITAN, NGC2). Residual pains (change alerts, terrain freshness) remain HYPOTHESIS/LOW after three research passes across G13, G03 and G31. TAK plugin economics are services-shaped (PAR acquired by Booz Allen). Analyst assessment: ACCEPTED; the only soft spot is that DHS S&T does fund TAK features through integrators, which supports a consultancy path, not a company.

competition.summary: The first named function is a free government plugin (UAS Tool shows footprint/SPI from KLV), the second is stock on the Army's company-level drone (Skydio Onboard Modeling) and the product of a funded, acquisitive vendor with ATAK export (Reveal Farsight, USSOCOM-developed), the 3D Tiles rendering and basemap packaging are on TPC/AGC's 2026 agenda, algorithms are open (OpenDroneMap/Obj2Tiles), and the distribution half is covered by TAK Server sync, CloudTAK, map-depot, AGC RBT and Ditto. The residual increments could be shipped by TPC, Reveal, Skydio or Ditto within one or two release cycles (INFERENCE, MEDIUM). Analyst assessment: ACCEPTED at full strength; this session added two independent confirmations (UAS Tool KLV overlay; Reveal ATAK export + Series B) beyond what the parent skeptics cited.

feasibility.summary: Technically and legally the unclassified MVP is feasible for this team on $250k (open data, ATAK-CIV, commercial hardware, likely EAR99/ENC - counsel to confirm), which is why founder fit scores 3.5. The refutation is about founder fit to the market rather than to the build: three fatal-if-absent roles are missing, SBIR is blocked by the ownership test until restructuring and the German founder's permanent residency, TAK-GOV/MIL and CUI data are gated for the non-U.S.-person founder if the defense variant is pursued, and the credible customer milestone requires a sponsor the team does not have. Analyst assessment: ACCEPTED at strength 3; this lens is the weakest of the three because the scope was deliberately built to pass it.

verdict_rationale: Kill. Decisive reason: this narrower form is a feature set inside a government-owned, free, services-priced ecosystem, and its named functions are already delivered by the ecosystem's owner or its funded occupants. Verified this session: ATAK with the government UAS Tool plugin already overlays the KLV sensor footprint and stare point on the map (FACT, MEDIUM; UAS Tool user guide mirror and Play listing), and public-safety agencies are adopting exactly that free stack (HSToday); Skydio Onboard Modeling builds a 3D mesh on the controller within minutes and X10D streams to ATAK offline (company-reported, MEDIUM); Reveal Farsight produces 2D/3D at the edge 'in moments', exports to ATAK, was built with USSOCOM, partnered with Maxar (2025-05-06) and raised a $30M Series B with acquisition intent (MEDIUM); TPC's TAK Offsite 2026 agenda carries a Cesium 3D Tiles program update and an AGC Releasable Basemap Tiles demo (FACT, HIGH); OpenDroneMap plus Obj2Tiles make the imagery-to-3D-Tiles pipeline free (FACT, HIGH). The distribution half was already refuted in G03 (TAK Server sync, CloudTAK, map-depot, AGC RBT, Ditto) and nothing new rescues it. The PROBLEM -> USER -> REQUIREMENT OWNER -> PROGRAM OFFICE -> CONTRACTING OFFICE -> BUDGET -> VEHICLE path breaks at REQUIREMENT OWNER and BUDGET (no office owns the function; Public evidence insufficient for any line), which triggers the major penalty. The residual increments (edge change-vs-baseline overlays; bandwidth-budgeted priority delta of 3D terrain across non-NGC2 federations) are genuine but small, have no named buyer, and sit on roadmaps controlled by TPC, AGC, Reveal, Skydio and Ditto. Founder fit (3.5) is the best of the three cards in this lineage because the scope is unclassified by construction, but that is necessary, not sufficient: market attractiveness is 2.1 and the outcome ceiling is an acqui-hire or a TAK services shop. Competition skeptic strength 5, market 4, feasibility 3; I could not rebut any with evidence. Confidence MEDIUM: several key facts come from search summaries of company pages and a mirrored manual rather than primary documents read in full, and the hstoday fetch was blocked.
narrower_version_if_borderline: Not recommended as a company. If the founders insist on the space, the only rational use of capital is a 3-month, under-$30k validation: publish an open-source ATAK-CIV plugin that adds change-vs-baseline overlays to whatever 3D the user already has (Skydio/Reveal/ODM output), instrument adoption, interview five wildfire/SAR/S2 users and one TPC engineer, and ask one state TAK program or one allied civil-protection agency whether it would pay for support. If that produces a paid pilot, run it as a bootstrapped TAK plugin-and-services shop with Reveal, Skydio or a TAK integrator as the exit; if not, stop. Do not raise venture money against it and do not restructure the cap table for SBIR on the strength of this gap alone.
most_important_question_answer: If two exceptionally capable founders had $250,000 today and insisted on this gap, they should build only the piece nobody ships free: an open-source ATAK-CIV plugin plus a Jetson edge service that takes any MISB KLV feed or drone photo set, produces incremental 3D Tiles with OpenDroneMap-class tooling, and computes a change-vs-baseline overlay with a confidence slider against the previous flight or an open terrain baseline, delta-synced across two federated TAK Servers over an emulated 64 kbit/s link - roughly $60-150k and four to six months with one contracted photogrammetry engineer. They would show it to a wildfire incident-management-team situation unit that already runs ATAK (the CAL FIRE/IMT-4 type user), a state TAK program lead (COTAK-type), a brigade S2 12Y cell, and one TAK Product Center engineer. The demo would prove measured georegistration error against RTK, time-to-tiles per hectare on a Jetson, change-detection precision/recall on a staged scene, and bytes/time-to-converge versus native TAK mission packages after an outage. The customer would care because today change is judged by eye and 3D arrives hours later unless they own a Skydio or a Reveal licence. The honest answer to the crush test is that no incumbent needs to crush them: the government already owns the free vendor-neutral layer and has 3D Tiles and basemap packaging on its 2026 agenda, Skydio ships onboard 3D, and Reveal - funded, USSOCOM-born and openly acquisitive - can add change overlays to a product that already exports to ATAK; the founders' only protection is speed to a widely installed open plugin, which is a recruiting asset, not a company. The milestone that would justify $2-5M does not exist in a form this scope can reach: it would require a signed, paid pilot with a named requirement owner (a PM MC, USSOCOM, DHS S&T or allied solicitation naming change-vs-baseline or bandwidth-prioritised terrain distribution as a distinct requirement) plus written confirmation from TPC that neither function is on the ATAK or TAK Server roadmap. Because three research passes found neither, and because the buyer's revealed price for the surrounding stack is zero, this fails as a venture and survives at most as a bootstrapped plugin-and-services effort with an acqui-hire exit.
bear_case_summary: Every named function is free (ATAK UAS Tool KLV footprint), stock (Skydio Onboard Modeling), funded (Reveal Farsight with ATAK export, $33.6M STRATFI, $30M Series B, acquisitive), government-roadmapped (TPC Cesium 3D Tiles, AGC Releasable Basemap Tiles, TAK Server sync, CloudTAK) or open source (OpenDroneMap/Obj2Tiles); no requirement owner or budget line exists; public-safety users adopt free stacks; TAK plugin economics are services-shaped (PAR acquired by Booz Allen); the residual increments are one release cycle from four incumbents; and the team lacks the three fatal roles and an SBIR-eligible cap table.
bull_case_summary: The scope is fully unclassified, buildable on open data and commercial hardware in months, keeps both founders engaged, sits on a 500,000-user government-owned distribution channel with public source, and targets two functions (edge change-vs-baseline overlays; bandwidth-budgeted priority delta of 3D terrain across non-NGC2 and allied federations) that no fielded product is evidenced to deliver; OWT production and DFR expansion multiply the 3D data and the drone flights involved; allied TAK users and German civil protection are a channel the German founder can open; and Reveal's stated acquisition appetite gives a plausible, if small, exit.
